body:
This shouldn't be called from Control. It will cause a RenderingServer stall every time that it is called.

In general the RenderingServer should never return data. You should only ever push data into the RenderingServer, never retrieve it
Alright, I'll see about doing it without that

I'm not sure about the knock-on effects of doing this. I think any control nodes rely on having precise control over their rect on the scene-side. This would introduce a situation where the scene is no longer aware of the size of the rect. 

I am thinking it may cause problems with things like containers that need to auto-balance their contents, or anchors which need to dynamically adjust to the size of the control node.

My gut feeling is that this change will have very far reaching consequences despite seemingly just being a fix for the `clip_children` setting. 

Maybe this should work more like what we do with the CanvasGroup node? Basically you can detect if a Canvasitem is a CanvasGroup owner, and then only change the rect size if it is

I've actually already anticipated and investigated this.
The `get_rect()` function and modifications of the rendering server canvas items luckily only affect the canvas item culling and rendering, not the actual rects used for the control workflow. This is because control nodes have their own `get_rect()` and related functions which only use the transform based rect.
Hence why `debug_canvas_item_get_rect()` on the rendering server differs from `get_rect()` on control nodes.

And for some amount of reassurance: I have tested this with both the [Control Gallery Demo Project](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/gui/control_gallery) and my own game project that I have been working on for roughly 2 years and have found no apparent issues in any GUI scene, be it the main menu or the gameplay menus, which make heavy use of containers and anchors with skewed styleboxes and styleboxes utilizing expand margins and drop shadows.

This also fixes more than just the `clip_children` issue, mainly:
- `CanvasGroup` not including the whole area of *any* control child that draws outside of its bounds.
- Controls that draw outside of the regular control rect getting culled when they shouldn't be. See this video using the master branch with a simple control script that draws a box using `draw_rect`:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fcd35808-db6b-4d3a-87fc-b5e6a8dd5d0f

*All of these issues occur for custom `_draw()` implementations too and have done so since Godot 4.0*.
On that note, I'm wondering if separate issues should be created for the other problems this PR solves.
